name: Restless scheduler (random jumps in a sigma window)
plain: Takes a sigma list and, inside a chosen step window, replaces the run of sigmas with a seeded random walk that picks sigmas from a window that shrinks from the high end by shrink_factor each pick. The output can go back up in sigma, so most multistep and history samplers break; the node's own description calls it a hack that works okay-ish with ping-pong. Sigmas before the window and after it are kept as they were.
math:
Symbols: s window sigmas (n of them); k pick count; f shrink_factor.
while W=int((n−1) − k·f) > 0: j ~ U{0..W} (j+1 if equal to the last j); append s[int(k·f)+j]; k+=1.
out = head + picks + tail.
